children.distinguishingFeatures: Unlike other flying animals like birds, bats have wings formed by skin stretched between extremely long finger bones, and they are the only flying mammals. Their wing structure allows for incredibly agile flight patterns that surpass most birds in maneuverability.
children.funFact: A single little brown bat can catch and eat over 1,000 mosquitoes in just one hour, making them incredibly effective natural pest controllers.

children.name: Lagomorpha
Leporidae
Sylvilagus
children.description: Cottontail rabbits are small to medium-sized mammals known for their fluffy white tails that look like cotton balls when they hop away. These rabbits are herbivores that feed on grasses, plants, and bark, and they're most active during dawn and dusk hours. They're excellent jumpers and can quickly zigzag through dense vegetation to escape predators.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Unlike their larger hare relatives, cottontail rabbits are born helpless with closed eyes and no fur, and they live in shallow ground nests rather than above-ground forms. Their ears are proportionally shorter than those of hares, and they prefer to hide rather than outrun predators in open areas.
children.funFact: Cottontail rabbits practice a behavior called coprophagy - they eat their own soft droppings to extract maximum nutrition from their plant-based diet, essentially digesting their food twice!

children.name: Lepus
children.description: Hares and jackrabbits in the genus Lepus are larger cousins of rabbits, built for speed and endurance in open habitats. They have longer legs, larger ears, and more muscular hind quarters than their rabbit relatives. These animals are known for their incredible jumping ability and quick bursts of speed to escape predators.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Unlike rabbits, hares are born fully furred with open eyes and are ready to hop around shortly after birth. They also tend to live above ground in shallow depressions rather than in burrows.
children.funFact: The Snowshoe Hare's feet act like natural snowshoes, spreading wide to distribute their weight and prevent them from sinking into deep snow - and they can change their fur color from brown in summer to white in winter for perfect camouflage!

children.name: Oryctolagus
children.description: European Rabbits are medium-sized mammals with long ears, powerful hind legs, and soft fur coats. They are herbivores that feed on grasses, herbs, and other plant materials, and are known for their impressive jumping ability and speed when escaping predators.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Unlike native cottontail rabbits, European Rabbits have longer ears relative to their body size and tend to be slightly larger overall. They also have different breeding behaviors, creating more elaborate burrow systems called warrens.
children.funFact: European Rabbits are not native to New England but were introduced from Europe, and they're actually the ancestors of all domestic rabbit breeds!

children.description: Hares and rabbits are small to medium-sized mammals with long ears, powerful hind legs, and fluffy tails. They are herbivores that feed on grasses, herbs, and other plant materials, and are well-known for their incredible jumping ability and quick reproductive rates. All members of this family have continuously growing front teeth that they must wear down by constant chewing.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Unlike rodents, leporids have two pairs of upper incisors (front teeth) instead of one pair. They also have much longer hind legs relative to their body size compared to most other small mammals, giving them their characteristic hopping gait.
children.funFact: Baby rabbits are born blind, deaf, and hairless in underground burrows, while baby hares are born fully furred with open eyes and can hop within hours of birth.

children.description: Lagomorphs are a small order of herbivorous mammals that includes rabbits, hares, and pikas. These animals are characterized by their continuously growing front teeth, powerful hind legs built for hopping or running, and plant-based diets. They're found in diverse habitats from grasslands to forests to rocky mountain slopes.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Unlike rodents, lagomorphs have two pairs of upper incisors (front teeth) instead of one pair, with a smaller second pair sitting directly behind the first. They also practice cecotrophy, eating special soft pellets of their own droppings to extract maximum nutrition from plant material.
children.funFact: Baby rabbits and hares develop very differently - rabbits are born blind, hairless, and helpless in underground burrows, while hares are born fully furred with open eyes and can hop within hours of birth.

children.name: Didelphimorphia
Didelphidae
Didelphis
children.description: Large American Opossums are the biggest marsupials found in the Americas, with cat-sized bodies and long, scaly tails. These nocturnal mammals are excellent climbers and have pouches where they carry their tiny babies after birth, just like kangaroos and other marsupials.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Unlike other North American mammals, these opossums have opposable thumbs on their hind feet and prehensile tails that can grip branches like an extra hand.
children.funFact: When threatened, opossums don't just 'play dead' - they actually enter an involuntary catatonic state complete with a slow heartbeat, shallow breathing, and even releasing a foul smell to convince predators they're already rotting!

children.description: Opossums are marsupials, meaning they carry and nurse their young in a pouch, making them unique among North American mammals. They are adaptable omnivores with grayish fur, hairless tails, and distinctive pointed snouts with many small teeth. These ancient mammals have remained relatively unchanged for millions of years.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Opossums are the only marsupials native to North America, setting them apart from all other local mammals that give birth to fully-developed young. They have opposable thumbs on their hind feet and prehensile tails that help them climb.
children.funFact: When threatened, opossums will 'play dead' by falling over, becoming limp, slowing their breathing, and even releasing a foul smell to convince predators they're already deceased!

children.description: Opossums are North America's only native marsupials, meaning they carry and nurse their young in a pouch like kangaroos do. These adaptable mammals are known for their ability to thrive in diverse habitats from forests to suburban areas. They are excellent climbers with opposable thumbs on their hind feet and prehensile tails that help them navigate through trees.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Unlike placental mammals, opossums give birth to tiny, underdeveloped young that must crawl into their mother's pouch to continue growing. They are the only marsupials found naturally in North America north of Mexico.
children.funFact: When threatened, opossums don't just pretend to be dead - they actually enter an involuntary catatonic state complete with slowed breathing, drooling, and even releasing a foul smell to make the act more convincing!

children.name: Sirenia
Trichechidae
Trichechus
children.description: Manatees are large, gentle marine mammals that live in warm coastal waters and rivers. They are completely aquatic herbivores with paddle-like flippers, rounded tails, and thick, wrinkled gray skin that helps them glide gracefully through the water.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Unlike seals or whales, manatees have no dorsal fin and possess a distinctive rounded, paddle-shaped tail rather than a forked one. They are the only fully aquatic mammals that are strict vegetarians.
children.funFact: Manatees are closely related to elephants and share a common ancestor, which explains their thick skin and slow, deliberate movements.

children.description: Manatees are large, gentle marine mammals that spend their lives in warm coastal waters and rivers. These peaceful giants are herbivores, using their paddle-like flippers to navigate shallow waters while grazing on seagrass and aquatic plants. They are slow-moving creatures perfectly adapted for an aquatic lifestyle.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Unlike other marine mammals, manatees have a rounded, paddle-shaped tail and no dorsal fin. They are the only completely aquatic mammals that are strict herbivores, spending most of their time grazing underwater.
children.funFact: Manatees are surprisingly related to elephants and share a common ancestor, which explains why they both have thick, wrinkled skin and continuously growing teeth!

children.description: Sirenians are large, gentle marine mammals that spend their entire lives in the water, feeding exclusively on plants like seagrasses and algae. These slow-moving giants have paddle-like flippers, no hind limbs, and a broad, flat tail that helps them navigate shallow coastal waters and rivers.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Unlike other marine mammals, sirenians are the only fully aquatic herbivores, making them unique among ocean dwellers. They have dense, heavy bones that help them stay submerged while grazing on underwater vegetation.
children.funFact: Sirenians are named after the mythical sirens because sailors long ago mistook these graceful creatures for mermaids when they saw them floating upright in the water.

children.name: Perissodactyla
Equidae
Equus
children.description: Equines are large, hoofed mammals belonging to the horse family, characterized by their single toe on each foot that forms a hard hoof. These powerful animals are built for running with long legs, muscular bodies, and flowing manes and tails. All members of this genus are herbivores that graze on grasses and other vegetation.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Equines are distinguished from other hoofed animals by having only one functional toe per foot (making them 'odd-toed ungulates') rather than the split hooves found in cattle, deer, and pigs. Their teeth are specially adapted for grinding tough plant material and continue growing throughout their lives.
children.funFact: Horses can sleep both lying down and standing up thanks to a special locking mechanism in their leg joints that allows them to rest without falling over.

children.description: Equines are hoofed mammals known for their single-toed feet, long legs, and flowing manes and tails. They are herbivorous animals that have evolved for running across open grasslands and have been domesticated by humans for thousands of years for transportation, work, and companionship.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Unlike other hoofed mammals, equines have only one functional toe on each foot (the hoof), while their ancestors had multiple toes that were gradually lost through evolution.
children.funFact: Horses can sleep both lying down and standing up thanks to a special locking mechanism in their legs that allows them to rest without falling over.

children.description: Odd-toed ungulates are hoofed mammals that bear their weight on an odd number of toes, typically one or three per foot. This ancient group includes horses, zebras, donkeys, tapirs, and rhinoceroses. They are herbivores with specialized digestive systems that help them break down tough plant material.
children.distinguishingFeatures: Unlike even-toed ungulates (like deer and cattle), these animals have their main weight-bearing axis running through the middle toe. Their hind gut fermentation system is also different from the multi-chambered stomachs of ruminants.
children.funFact: Despite having only about 17 species alive today, odd-toed ungulates were once incredibly diverse, with over 130 different species roaming the Earth millions of years ago.
